blocks.text: Practice long questions for the whole of Unit 4 (Matrices & Determinants), in the shape of a Board Section-II question part: each carries 5 marks (a longer problem, a proof or a derivation). Each one is solved in full, step by step.

blocks.prompt: 1 If \(A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 & 0 \\ 3 & 4 & 1\end{bmatrix}\) and \(B = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & -2 & 5\end{bmatrix}\), show that \((A - B)^{t} = A^{t} - B^{t}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Work out each side separately: subtract then transpose; transpose then subtract; compare.

book_ref.quote: The same is true for a difference

steps: (i) and (ii) have the same order \(3 \times 2\) and equal corresponding entries

blocks.prompt: 2 If \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}\), find the matrix \(X\) such that \(A^{2} - 3A + 2I - X = O\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: \(X = A^{2} - 3A + 2I\); find \(A^{2} = A \cdot A\) row by column, then combine entry by entry.

book_ref.quote: Powers exist only for square matrices

blocks.prompt: 3 Verify the left distributive property \(A(B + C) = AB + AC\) for \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}\), \(C = \begin{bmatrix}-1 & 2 \\ 4 & 1\end{bmatrix}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Compute the left side (add, then multiply) and the right side (multiply twice, then add); keep A on the left throughout.

book_ref.quote: Left distributive property

blocks.prompt: 4 For \(A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 1 & -1 \\ 3 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 & 1\end{bmatrix}\), find all nine cofactors. Hence find \(|A|\) by expanding along \(R_{1}\) and along \(C_{3}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: \(A_{ij} = (-1)^{i+j}M_{ij}\) with the chessboard signs; then (element) \(\times\) (its cofactor), added, along any line.

book_ref.quote: These are used again in 4.4.2

blocks.prompt: 5 Find the values of \(x\) for which \(\begin{vmatrix}x & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & x & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & x\end{vmatrix} = 0\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Expand along the first row (it has a zero), factorise the cubic and solve.

book_ref.quote: is the required expansion of determinant of square matrix of order 3

steps: Expand along \(R_{1}\): \(\begin{vmatrix}x & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & x & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & x\end{vmatrix} = x\begin{vmatrix}x & 1 \\ 1 & x\end{vmatrix} - 1\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 0 & x\end{vmatrix} + 0\)

blocks.prompt: 6 Without expansion, show that \(\begin{vmatrix}a & b & c \\ b + c & c + a & a + b \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{vmatrix} = 0\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Make two rows identical with the properties: add R1 to R2, take the common factor out, and compare with R3.

book_ref.quote: Two uses of v: a common factor of a row or column can be taken outside the determinant

steps: \(R_{2} + R_{1} \to R_{2}\) (property vii, value unchanged): \(R_{2}\) becomes \((a + b + c,\ a + b + c,\ a + b + c)\)
\(= \begin{vmatrix}a & b & c \\ a + b + c & a + b + c & a + b + c \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{vmatrix}\)
Take \(a + b + c\) out of \(R_{2}\) (property v): \(= (a + b + c)\begin{vmatrix}a & b & c \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{vmatrix}\)
\(R_{2}\) and \(R_{3}\) are identical, so the determinant is \(0\) (property iii)

blocks.prompt: 7 Show that \(\begin{vmatrix}1 + a & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 + b & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 + c\end{vmatrix} = abc + ab + bc + ca\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Create zeros with row operations (value unchanged), then expand along the row with a zero.

book_ref.quote: This is how zeros are created before expanding.

steps: \(R_{1} - R_{3} \to R_{1}\), \(R_{2} - R_{3} \to R_{2}\) (property vii): \(\begin{vmatrix}a & 0 & -c \\ 0 & b & -c \\ 1 & 1 & 1 + c\end{vmatrix}\)
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: the determinant \(= abc + ab + bc + ca\)

blocks.prompt: 8 Show that \(\begin{vmatrix}x & y & x + y \\ y & x + y & x \\ x + y & x & y\end{vmatrix} = -2(x^{3} + y^{3})\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Each row adds up to 2(x + y): collect it in the first column, take it out, make zeros and expand.

book_ref.quote: Adding \(k\) times one row (column) to another: value unchanged

steps: \(C_{1} + C_{2} + C_{3} \to C_{1}\) (property vii): every entry of \(C_{1}\) becomes \(2(x + y)\)
Take \(2(x + y)\) out of \(C_{1}\): \(= 2(x + y)\begin{vmatrix}1 & y & x + y \\ 1 & x + y & x \\ 1 & x & y\end{vmatrix}\)

blocks.prompt: 9 Find \(A^{-1}\) by the adjoint method if \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 4\end{bmatrix}\), and verify that \(AA^{-1} = I_{3}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: \(A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj} A\): determinant, nine cofactors, transpose, divide, check.

book_ref.quote: Find all nine cofactors \(A_{ij} = (-1)^{i+j}M_{ij}\).

blocks.explanation: Find |A| and the adjoint, then multiply: each diagonal entry should be |A| and every other entry 0.

blocks.explanation: Check \(|A| \ne 0\), then reduce \(A \vdots I_{3}\) to \(I_{3} \vdots A^{-1}\), applying every operation to the whole row.

blocks.prompt: 12 Reduce \(\begin{bmatrix}2 & 4 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 7 & 0 & 8\end{bmatrix}\) to echelon form and to reduced echelon form. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Get a leading 1 in each row and zeros below it (echelon); then clear the entries above every leading 1 (reduced).

book_ref.quote: Echelon form is enough to find a rank

blocks.prompt: 13 Find the rank of \(\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 & 3 \\ 3 & 0 & 3 & 3\end{bmatrix}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Reduce to echelon form and count the non-zero rows.

book_ref.quote: The rank counts how many rows carry genuinely new information.

blocks.explanation: Reduce the whole augmented matrix (constants included) until the coefficient part is the identity; then read the last column.

blocks.prompt: 15 Show that the system \(x + y - z = 2,\ 2x + 3y + z = 7,\ 3x + 4y = 9\) is consistent and find its general solution. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Reduce the augmented matrix, compare the two ranks with the number of variables, and write the free variable as t.

book_ref.quote: In system (ii), the rank of the coefficient matrix is the same as that of the augmented matrix

steps: Rank of coefficient matrix = rank of augmented matrix = 2 < 3: consistent, infinitely many solutions
blocks.final_answer: \(x = 4t - 1,\ y = 3 - 3t,\ z = t\) for any real \(t\)

blocks.prompt: 16 Use the matrix inversion method to solve \(x + 2y = -1,\ 2x + 5y + z = -1,\ y + 2z = 3\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Write \(AX = B\), check \(|A| \ne 0\), find \(A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj} A\), then \(X = A^{-1}B\).

blocks.explanation: \(x_{k} = \dfrac{D_{k}}{|A|}\): replace column \(k\) of \(|A|\) by the constants; first check \(|A| \ne 0\).

blocks.prompt: 18 For the system \(a_{i1}x_{1} + a_{i2}x_{2} + a_{i3}x_{3} = b_{i}\) (\(i = 1, 2, 3\)) with \(|A| \ne 0\), derive Cramer's rule. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Start from \(X = A^{-1}B\) with \(A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj} A\) and recognise each numerator as a determinant expanded along a column.

book_ref.quote: We have already proved that

steps: Write the system as \(AX = B\); if \(|A| \ne 0\), \(X = A^{-1}B = \dfrac{1}{|A|}(\operatorname{adj} A)B\)
\(x_{1} = \dfrac{b_{1}A_{11} + b_{2}A_{21} + b_{3}A_{31}}{|A|}\); \(A_{11}, A_{21}, A_{31}\) are the cofactors of column 1 and do not contain column 1
So the numerator is the expansion along column 1 of \(\begin{vmatrix}b_{1} & a_{12} & a_{13} \\ b_{2} & a_{22} & a_{23} \\ b_{3} & a_{32} & a_{33}\end{vmatrix} = D_{1}\)
In the same way \(x_{2}\) has numerator \(b_{1}A_{12} + b_{2}A_{22} + b_{3}A_{32} = D_{2}\) (column 2 replaced) and \(x_{3}\) has \(D_{3}\) (column 3 replaced)

blocks.prompt: 19 Solve by Gaussian elimination: \(x + 2y - z = 0,\ 2x + y + z = 0,\ x - y + 2z = 0\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Reduce the augmented matrix to row-echelon form, read the rank, and back-substitute with a free variable.

book_ref.quote: It involves performing a series of row operations on the system's augmented matrix

steps: Row-echelon form has 2 non-zero rows: rank of \(A = 2 < 3\), so non-trivial solutions exist (Rule II)
Back substitution: \(y - z = 0 \Rightarrow y = z\); \(x + 2y - z = 0 \Rightarrow x = -2z + z = -z\); put \(z = t\)
blocks.final_answer: \(x = -t,\ y = t,\ z = t\) for any \(t\) (non-trivial for \(t \ne 0\))

blocks.explanation: Non-trivial solutions need rank less than 3, i.e. \(|A| = 0\); find \(\lambda\), then solve by Gaussian elimination.

blocks.prompt: 21 A triangle has vertices \(P(1, 4)\), \(Q(-3, 2)\) and \(R(5, -1)\). Find the vertices of its reflection in the line \(y = x\) using a transformation matrix. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Write each vertex as a 2 x 1 column and multiply it on the left by the reflection matrix of y = x.

book_ref.quote: Transformation or Reflection Matrix is a mathematical tool

steps: Reflection in \(y = x\) uses \(\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}\); write each vertex as a column
Check: reflection in \(y = x\) swaps the coordinates: \((1, 4) \to (4, 1)\), \((-3, 2) \to (2, -3)\), \((5, -1) \to (-1, 5)\)

blocks.prompt: 22 Use \(A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}\) to encode the message HELP (A to Z = 1 to 26), and decode the result to check it. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Change letters to numbers, group them in twos as \(2 \times 1\) columns, multiply each by \(A\); decode with \(A^{-1}\).

book_ref.quote: It is often used to hide the actual meaning of a message.

steps: HELP in groups of two: HE, LP; H = 8, E = 5, L = 12, P = 16: \(\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}, \begin{bmatrix}12 \\ 16\end{bmatrix}\)
